_comment: ⚑ THE PreToolUse HOOKS ARE ARMED, AND THE ARMING IS ON THE COMMAND LINE.
An env block alone is correct and INSUFFICIENT: a session already running when this
file changes never picks it up, so the hooks keep exiting 0 — detecting every violation
and reporting none. That is the worst pairing, a guard that reads as armed in review and
is off in fact (measured in el-openglo, reported as armed for several commits).
ADVISORY MODE IS SILENT TO THE AGENT, not merely non-blocking: unarmed, a hook prints its
advisory and exits 0 with no permissionDecision, which the harness reads as 'allow,
nothing to report' — the text reaches nobody. So the choice is guard or no guard.
ADOPTED, NOT INVENTED. hook_structural_query / hook_no_chaining / hook_cmdparse are
SYMLINKS into ../substrate/scripts/ (the route linux-sources, summit, freecell and gabion
took). hook_gate_running.py is linux-sources' and is held as a real file. Ownership is
not claimed for any of them. They read THIS repo's routing table at
.claude/skills/struct-tools/SKILL.md, which must stay a REAL LOCAL FILE.
WHY THIS REPO NEEDS hook_gate_running PARTICULARLY: //:hook is a 126k-action sweep that
runs up to ~2h on an engine-source change. A tracked-tree edit mid-run reds sandboxed
cells with 'input dependency modified during execution', which reads as an engine defect
and costs the whole sweep. Recorded as Λ·quiesce after ~7 occurrences; a memory is a
stamp, and a stamp only tells you the run was worthless once it finishes.
⚑ THE FIFTH HOOK IS hook_shellcheck (Ζ·hook·shellcheck, armed 2026-08-30), adopted by
symlink from substrate — the same file linux-sources and cassian-observability run. It
matches BOTH Bash and Edit|Write|NotebookEdit, because shell reaches this repo by two
routes: a command the agent runs, and a script the agent WRITES.
IT GATES MEANING, WHICH THE OTHER FOUR DO NOT. structural-query and no-chaining refuse a
textual query over a structured artifact and a composed command — both about SHAPE.
Neither reads what the shell DOES. Cassian's line for the class: `[ $x = y ]` with an
empty x and `rm -rf $TARGET/*` with TARGET unset passed both.
THE TREE WAS CLEANED TO 0 BEFORE ARMING, per cassian's rule — arming first would make the
shell un-editable by the session that has to clean it. 15 files, 10 findings, all resolved
and NONE excluded: one genuine fix (tools/toolchain_status.sh parsed `ls` output for the
veraPDF JAR; a shell glob needs no subprocess and tests absence rather than inferring it
from a swallowed error), two intentional word-splits carrying disable directives that state
the mechanism ($PK_BES is empty-or-two-flags; $_pk_extra is a path LIST, and quoting it
would reintroduce the very leak its trap prevents), two SC2329 false positives (functions
invoked indirectly through `declare -f` into a flock subshell — shellcheck says so itself),
and one REAL portability finding kept as a finding: /dev/tcp is bash and .githooks/pre-commit
is #!/bin/sh, so under dash the telemetry probe reports DOES NOT ANSWER for LIVE endpoints.
Filed Ζ·probe·portable. A disable directive records that a limit is known; it does not make
the code portable.
⚑ AND THE THREE assets/*.sh CARRY SHEBANGS RATHER THAN AN EXCLUSION (operator ruling,
2026-08-30: *above anything else, our examples and recommendations ought to be
well-formed*). They are emit: fragments projected into README.md — two-line command
examples a reader COPIES. Excluding them as documentation was the easy call and the wrong
one: an unverified example in a published document is the same defect this engine refuses
one layer up, and the shebang also tells the reader which shell the commands are valid in.
⚑ THE SIXTH HOOK IS hook_pycheck (ruff AND mypy in ONE hook, armed 2026-08-30), adopted by
symlink. It matches Edit|Write|NotebookEdit only — Python is never a Bash-command concern.
IT IS ARMED AGAINST AN UNCLEAN TREE, DELIBERATELY, AND THAT IS NOT CASSIAN'S RULE BROKEN.
Their clean-then-arm rule is right for a WHOLE-TREE gate; this one is PER-FILE-ON-EDIT, and
the difference is load-bearing. MEASURED BEFORE ARMING: with 6,955 findings in the backlog, a
CLEAN file is allowed and a DIRTY one is refused. So the backlog and the gate never meet until
you open a file — at which point the refusal IS the work. linux-sources named the method:
*the gate doesn't tell you to clean the monolith, it tells you the monolith is too big to
touch; the only move is to decompose*. They dissolved two monoliths (910 and 1315 lines) into
~10 small one-concern modules each, every one written clean in one pass. The big number is
never eaten because it is never confronted as a number.
⚑ IT CRASHED ON FIRST ADOPTION, AND THE FIX CAME FROM UPSTREAM WHILE THIS WAS BEING WRITTEN.
`from scripts import hook_shellcheck` raised ModuleNotFoundError at MODULE LOAD in a repo
whose scripts/ is a bare symlink directory — and empty stdout is read by the harness as ALLOW,
so the hook denied NOTHING while reading as armed. Reported to substrate with the traceback;
they added a _ROOT prelude plus a loud ImportError arm, and found the sharper thing: three
sibling hooks ALREADY carried that prelude and this one was the MISSED MEMBER OF A SET.
⚑⚑ WHICH IS WHY THESE STAY SYMLINKS AND WERE NOT VENDORED. Vendoring was considered and
rejected ON MEASUREMENT: the crash was the only reason to fork, and the symlink is what
delivered the repair with zero action here. A vendored copy would still be broken. The cost is
real and accepted — a symlink adopter inherits upstream's bugs as well as its fixes, and
substrate's tree is red and uncommitted as this lands.
VERIFY BY MAKING IT FIRE, NEVER BY READING THIS FILE.
